subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WebSocket origin gate reusing checkBrowserOrigin

question: Should the Gateway apply its existing `gateway.controlUi` browser-origin policy before HTTP 101 for every browser-originated WebSocket upgrade, instead of retaining post-handshake rejection semantics?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, but it deliberately moves a security and compatibility boundary earlier in the connection lifecycle; repository policy treats changed startup/fallback/admission behavior as maintainer-visible compatibility risk.

options.title: Adopt pre-handshake enforcement
options.body: Approve the earlier 403 rejection once the current head has exact raw-handshake proof for allowed and rejected cases.

options.title: Keep post-handshake behavior
options.body: Retain the existing admission timing if compatibility with clients or intermediaries that observe an upgraded connection is required.

options.title: Define a distinct Gateway policy
options.body: Request a separately documented configuration or migration only if Gateway owners need pre-handshake origin enforcement to differ from the current Control UI policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt pre-handshake enforcement
recommendation.body: Approve the earlier 403 rejection once the current head has exact raw-handshake proof for allowed and rejected cases.

likelyOwner.reason: Timeline activity is the only available direct maintainer-routing signal for this Gateway security decision.
